title: Reduce reactions to accidental peanut exposure through oral immunotherapy

concept.text: Raise the reaction threshold in peanut-allergic patients through standardized oral desensitisation. This reduces risk during ongoing treatment but does not establish permanent, treatment-free tolerance. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for mitigation of reactions after accidental exposure, supported by a randomized phase 3 food-challenge trial demonstrating an increased proportion tolerating a 600 mg peanut-protein challenge after approximately one year of treatment. Test set by: FDA; the PALISADE/ARC003 programme used controlled oral challenge as a surrogate for mitigation of accidental-exposure reactions. Reported achieved: FDA approved Palforzia on 31 January 2020. Overlaps: CLM-01, IMM-04, PHA-04, DER-07. Sources given: [FDA Palforzia approval record](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/allergenics/palforzia) ; [FDA Palforzia regulatory assessment](https://www.fda.gov/media/135328/download).

page.title: Peanut oral immunotherapy for desensitisation
page.definition: Children with peanut allergy receive increasing doses of peanut protein followed by daily maintenance, raising the amount they can ingest without dose-limiting allergic symptoms. This on-treatment effect is called desensitisation; it does not establish tolerance after treatment stops.

goal.need: FDA's estimates published on 31 January 2020 put childhood peanut allergy in the United States at approximately 1 million cases, with natural resolution in about 20%. Avoidance leaves a continuing need for protection against accidental ingestion. Oral immunotherapy addresses this by increasing the reaction threshold during treatment.

figures.caption: FDA estimates published on 31 January 2020
figures.note: These describe disease burden and natural history, not treatment outcomes.

statements.body: European Academy of Allergy and Clinical Immunology
statements.quote: In children and adolescents with IgE-mediated peanut allergy, peanut oral immunotherapy is recommended to achieve desensitisation.

completion.title: FDA licenses a peanut oral immunotherapy to mitigate reactions following accidental peanut exposure.
completion.criterion: FDA grants a biologics licence for an oral peanut-allergen product indicated to mitigate allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, after accidental peanut exposure, with the required safety controls. Achieved on 31 January 2020: FDA licensed Palforzia, initially permitting treatment initiation at ages 4–17 years and continued treatment from age 4 years, alongside peanut avoidance and a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Palforzia biologics licence approval letter dated 31 January 2020.
completion.threshold_quote: We are issuing Department of Health and Human Services U.S. License No. 2109 to Aimmune Therapeutics, Inc., Brisbane, CA,
completion.basis: Licensure establishes the intended accidental-exposure indication. FDA accepted oral food challenge as a surrogate for that benefit and required controls for treatment-induced anaphylaxis. Nonclinical studies were not required because the active ingredient was food-grade peanut powder.

milestones.title: Peanut-allergic children tolerate 3.9 g cumulative peanut protein after oral immunotherapy.
milestones.criterion: In the Jones et al. open-label protocol, complete an oral challenge of 300, 600, 1200 and 1800 mg peanut protein, given 30 minutes apart, after maintenance at 300 mg/day. The challenge stops at 3.9 g total or with objective symptoms. Reported in 2009: 27 of 29 challenged children, from 39 enrolled, reached 3.9 g with no more than mild symptoms. Maintenance before challenge lasted 4–22 months.
milestones.set_by: Duke University Medical Center and Arkansas Children's Hospital investigators, Jones et al.'s published peanut oral immunotherapy protocol.
milestones.threshold_quote: The OFC was discontinued at 3.9 g or with objective symptoms.

milestones.title: A phase 2 trial demonstrates desensitisation to 443 mg cumulative peanut protein with standardised therapy.
milestones.criterion: In ARC001, compare the proportions tolerating at least 443 mg cumulative peanut protein with no or mild symptoms at the exit double-blind, placebo-controlled food challenge, after escalation to 300 mg/day. Eligible participants were aged 4–26 years. Published online on 31 October 2017: 23/29 AR101 recipients versus 5/26 placebo recipients met this endpoint, P < 0.0001. Six AR101 recipients withdrew.
milestones.set_by: Aimmune Therapeutics and ARC001 investigators, primary endpoint of the registered phase 2 study NCT01987817, published by Bird et al.
milestones.threshold_quote: able to tolerate ≥443 mg (cumulative peanut protein) at exit DBPCFC with no or mild symptoms.

milestones.title: A phase 3 peanut challenge trial exceeds a 15-percentage-point lower confidence bound for benefit.
milestones.criterion: In PALISADE/ARC003 participants aged 4–17 years, the lower 95% confidence bound for the treatment-minus-placebo responder difference must exceed 15 percentage points. Responders tolerate a single dose of at least 600 mg peanut protein, 1043 mg cumulative, with no more than mild symptoms at a double-blind, placebo-controlled challenge after 24 weeks of maintenance at 300 mg/day. Published on 18 November 2018: 250/372 AR101 recipients versus 5/124 placebo recipients responded; difference 63.2 percentage points, 95% confidence interval 53.0–73.3.
milestones.set_by: Aimmune Therapeutics, PALISADE/ARC003 prespecified efficacy criterion, documented in FDA's regulatory assessment.
milestones.threshold_quote: lower bound of the 95% CI of the difference in proportions of responders (PALFORZIA minus placebo) was greater than 15%.

results.finding: ARC001 (55 participants): 23/29 AR101 recipients versus 5/26 placebo recipients tolerated at least 443 mg of peanut protein.
results.detail: Participants were aged 4–26 years and escalated to 300 mg/day. The exit challenge required no or mild symptoms; P < .0001. Six AR101 recipients withdrew.
results.quote: In the intention-to-treat analysis, 23 of 29 (79%) and 18 of 29 (62%) AR101 subjects tolerated ≥443 mg and 1043 mg at exit DBPCFC, respectively, versus 5 of 26 (19%) and 0 of 26 (0%) placebo subjects (both P < .0001).

results.finding: FDA licensed Palforzia on 31 January 2020; sample size not applicable.
results.detail: Initial dose escalation was approved for ages 4–17; up-dosing and maintenance could continue from age 4. Peanut avoidance and an approved REMS were required.
results.quote:
Under this license, you are authorized to manufacture the product Peanut (Arachis 
hypogaea) Allergen Powder-dnfp, which is indicated for the mitigation of allergic 
reactions, including anaphylaxis, that may occur with accidental exposure to peanut.
